3d.tooltip.advanced_settings_1eb415: Open the optional seed control for this 3D render.
3d.tooltip.choose_a_reference_image_c700: Choose one image to guide the 3D model. TRELLIS.2 requires a transparent PNG or WebP unless you remove the background first; Hunyuan also accepts JPEG.
3d.tooltip.creative_notes_draft_only_a50: These notes are saved with the draft, but are not sent to either 3D model.
3d.tooltip.denoising_steps_d51281: Sets how many refinement steps the model runs. More steps can take longer; Hunyuan’s default is 30 and TRELLIS.2’s is 12.
3d.tooltip.describe_the_object_43f9a6: The object to create. Forge first draws it with Qwen Image 2.1 on a transparent background and saves that picture in your project, then builds the 3D model from it. Describe one object, fully in view.
3d.tooltip.guidance_scale_374a8f: How strongly Hunyuan follows the reference image, from 1 to 20. The default of 5 is the model’s own setting; higher values can look harsher.
3d.tooltip.image_seed_d839c5: Whole number that repeats the picture with the same description and steps. Leave empty for a random seed. The 3D seed is under Advanced settings.
3d.tooltip.image_steps_04c1d7: Refinement steps for the Qwen Image picture that the 3D model is built from, from 1 to 100. The default is 25. More steps take longer. The 3D step has its own settings below.
3d.tooltip.octree_resolution_4dc817: Sets the grid density of Hunyuan’s shape mesh. 128 is tested; 256 and 384 are experimental, add detail and triangles, and use more memory and time.
3d.tooltip.paint_texture_experimental_22: Adds a second Hunyuan stage that paints colour and metallic-roughness maps from your reference image. It loads extra models and takes much longer, and seams or soft detail can remain. There is no normal map. Leave it off for the tested untextured shape.
3d.tooltip.painted_views_advanced_e11fa7: How many views the Hunyuan painter renders and combines into the texture. The painter was trained on 6; more views take longer.
3d.tooltip.pipeline_a4a986: TRELLIS.2 resolution. 512 is the default and the fastest; 1024, 1024 cascade and 1536 cascade add detail but take longer, wait for more GPU memory and read about 5 GB of extra checkpoints the first time. On this computer one simple object took about 1 minute at 512, 4 minutes at 1024 and 1024 cascade, and 9 minutes at 1536 cascade.
3d.tooltip.reference_image_4fa20a: The single image the model uses to build the 3D asset. Hunyuan accepts PNG, JPEG, or WebP and treats any transparent pixels as background, so cut the object out first. TRELLIS.2 requires a transparent PNG or WebP. Tick “Remove the background first” to let Forge cut the object out with SAM 3.1 instead.
3d.tooltip.remove_the_background_first_u: Queues two renders: SAM 3.1 cuts out the object you name (saved as a transparent PNG in the project), then the 3D model is built from the cutout. Forge frees SAM 3.1 before loading the 3D model when it can (when it started SAM 3.1, nothing else is using it and no other queued render needs it). Unavailable when the picture already has a transparent background, because there is nothing to remove.
3d.tooltip.seed_d07208: Enter a whole number to help repeat a render with the same model and settings. Leave blank for a random seed.
3d.tooltip.texture_map_size_175564: Sets the size of the painted Hunyuan texture maps. 2048 holds more detail than 1024 and makes a larger file.
3d.tooltip.texture_size_4cca98: Sets the texture image size for TRELLIS.2. Larger textures can take longer and use more memory.
3d.tooltip.triangle_budget_ad930f: Optional mesh simplification. Automatic keeps Hunyuan’s raw mesh, or reduces it to 40,000 triangles when painting. TRELLIS.2 defaults to 100,000 triangles instead of the upstream 1,000,000. Fewer triangles suit games but lose detail.
3d.tooltip.view_size_advanced_4526cb: Size of each painted view in pixels. In a test here, 8 views at 768 pixels looked no better than 6 at 512, took about twice as long and used about 15 GB more GPU memory.
3d.tooltip.what_to_isolate_fc8cb3: A short description of the object SAM 3.1 should keep, for example “the dragon”. Name the thing in a word or two (“apple”, “knight”); generic words such as “object” often match nothing. Leave empty for “main object”, which works on many but not all pictures. If nothing matches, the 3D render stops with that message.
3d.tooltip.x1024_px_b18e61: Sets the TRELLIS.2 texture size to 1024 pixels. Larger textures can take longer and use more memory.
3d.tooltip.x128_tested_618e71: Uses Hunyuan’s tested mesh resolution. Higher resolutions are experimental and may need more memory and time.
3d.tooltip.x2048_px_835f4b: Sets the largest listed TRELLIS.2 texture size. It may take longer and use more memory.
3d.tooltip.x256_experimental_ac6ed4: Attempts a more detailed mesh with Hunyuan. This setting is experimental and may use more memory and time.
3d.tooltip.x384_experimental_63a486: Attempts the highest listed mesh detail with Hunyuan. This setting is experimental and may use substantially more memory and time.
3d.tooltip.x3d_model_946da7: Choose which model makes the 3D asset. Hunyuan creates an untextured shape by default and can optionally paint a texture (experimental); TRELLIS.2 makes a textured model from a transparent image and is experimental. Both save a GLB, which the asset library can convert to OBJ, PLY, STL or glTF.
3d.tooltip.x512_px_6f0e70: Sets the TRELLIS.2 texture size to 512 pixels. The textured model is experimental.
